messages.summary:
## Objective
- Enhance the existing WILDSHARD game with diagonal battle positioning, cookie-based save/resume, instant battle victories, a DS-style second-screen area, and clear creature type and move information.
- Generate creatures and moves procedurally by floor, then test the game and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing playable game and make reasonable assumptions without asking questions.
- Save progress across page refreshes using cookies.
- Battles must end as soon as the opponent’s health reaches zero.
- Remake the out-of-bounds area as a second screen inspired by DS games.
- Explain attacks and show creature types.
- Generate new creatures and moves procedurally by floor.
- Test gameplay and capture a small JPEG screenshot.

## Decisions
- The game is a single-page implementation in `index.html`; existing creature types are BLOOM, EMBER, TIDE, and DUSK.
- Implemented out-of-bounds traversal as wrap-around, with a field radar presented as a second screen in the side panel.
- Floor-generated species and moves draw from each type’s name fragments, move fragments, and palettes.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added an enemy type label and ally type label to the battle UI.
- Added DS-inspired field radar showing player, enemies, obstacles, and exit.
- Changed battle creature WebGL positioning toward opposite diagonal corners.
- Added cookie save/restore helpers and calls around UI updates, battle changes, and movement.
- Added procedural species names and floor-specific move generation with power and description fields.
- Changed enemy-zero-HP handling to call `winBattle()` immediately instead of delaying victory.

### Active
- Verify and fix save/restore behavior, especially active-battle restoration.
- Test gameplay and capture/read the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html` for syntax/runtime issues and fix restore behavior; generated enemies currently appear not to have unique `id` values, although battle saves restore by `enemyId`.
2. Run the game and verify movement, floor transitions, procedurally generated moves/species, battle types/descriptions, instant victory, and cookie resume.
3. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; all current changes are here.

## Important Context
- Cookie state is split across cookies using `wildshard_parts` and `wildshard_save_<index>`; battle persistence stores only the enemy ID.
- `restoreGame()` resets the random generator from the original seed, and battle-turn timing/state is not preserved.
- No gameplay tests or screenshot have been performed yet.

Verified movement and floor transitions, procedural creatures and moves, battle UI and instant victories, and save/resume—including restoring an active battle. Chromium tests reported no runtime errors; the screenshot is a 1280×900 JPEG.
